attacks.claim: Retrieval collections holding chunks and embeddings derived from customer documents are provisioned in us-east-2, outside the EU that the agreed DPA requires. Dual-write in week 2 extends this breach, and the plan has no residency control, waiver, or fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: The agreed release gate for any model change is the 4,100-case regression suite, but it is moved to week 6+ after week-4 cutover, so the changed model and prompts reach all tenants unvalidated. The 25-question blind comparison cannot substitute for it.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the A100 reservation and deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before the week-4 cutover and before any regression result. These are one-way actions, and a failed cutover or residency issue has no path back to the prior model.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle) and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Week 5 removes pgvector, vLLM manifests, and the GPU node pool before the week 6+ regression run, so no fallback exists while quality and retrieval reliability are unvalidated.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: LoRA per-practice behaviour is replaced by week-1 system prompts with no per-practice equivalence test. Adapters are deleted before any comparison could run, and the 25-question sample may not cover all practice areas.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Dual-write during week 2 mixes pgvector embeddings with 1,536-dim embed-3 vectors in different embedding spaces. The plan has no routing, index-version handling, or reconciliation rule, so mixed-state retrieval can return wrong or inconsistent chunks.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: Generation is pinned to eu-west-1 while retrieval is in us-east-2, so one tenant request splits across regions. The plan does not say where retrieved chunks inserted into prompts are processed.
attacks.evidence: "region eu-west-1 (Dublin)" alongside "currently provisioned in us-east-2"

attacks.claim: The parity claim overreaches. 25 support-inbox questions from two raters cannot confirm parity for legal QA across practice areas, and the tally (19 preferred + 3 tied of 25) leaves 3 unaccounted for with no rubric.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3. This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: The latency figure covers only p95 TTFT from Frankfurt over one week. It excludes end-to-end latency, the us-east-2 retrieval hop, and the long-context load that caused the OOM pages.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is attested only for org-level generation. Retention for embed-3 calls, Vector Store contents, and logs is unverified, and the embed-3 endpoint region is not specified even though embeddings are customer-derived.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." and "Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers."

attacks.claim: Adding Nimbus as a sub-processor of client documents for EU law firms likely requires DPA notice or customer consent. The timeline and risks have no such step.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no sub-processor notification, DPA amendment, or customer-notice step in the timeline or risks.

attacks.claim: Retrieval depends on a public-preview managed store with no stated SLA, failover, or alerting. Pgvector is removed in week 5, so a vendor outage becomes a total retrieval outage.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2"

attacks.claim: All tenants cut over at once in week 4 with no canary, staged rollout, or defined rollback trigger.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)."

attacks.claim: Re-embedding about 41M chunks has no stated batch size or throughput estimate. At 120 req/s with one chunk per request it alone takes roughly 4 days, and the plan does not say whether embedding, generation, and vector queries share one rate pool, which could starve live traffic.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus rate limits: our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: The $7,900 generation figure has no token-volume, price, or context-length basis. Re-embedding and dual-run costs are omitted, so the $9,550 total is not a budget.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900"

attacks.claim: Re-embedding 41M chunks into a proprietary space and vector store, while deleting the weights and adapters and removing the self-hosting Terraform, creates high exit cost and removes the ability to self-host again. No exit path is recorded.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation relies on a tenant-scoped client key, but server-side collection scoping and offboarding deletion are not described. Retrieved document text entering prompts has no prompt-injection mitigation.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Six weeks with three engineers cannot cover the 41M-chunk re-embed, dual-write, prompt rewrites, regression gate, cutover, and teardown. Validation falls after the deadline, and there are no go/no-go criteria.
attacks.evidence: "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: Rotating many tenant-scoped keys every 30 days has no described revocation or leak-detection process.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus API keys live in Vault, injected per pod, rotated every 30 days"

attacks.claim: No alerting, SLO, or on-call plan is defined for the new managed generation or retrieval dependency.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no observability, alerting, or failure-mode section for Nimbus generation or retrieval.
